data.long_meaning: Dhanvantari is the god of medicine and Ayurveda in Hindu mythology. The name Dhanvant carries the meaning “God of Medicine” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhanvant usually hope their child will grow to embody god of medicine and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dhanvant is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and is named after Lord Dhanvantari, the divine healing deity who is believed to have emerged during the Samudra Manthan, or the churning of the ocean. This event is significant in Hindu mythology as it led to the creation of various sacred materials essential for the existence of the world. Lord Dhanvantari holds the text of Ayurveda, the ancient Indian system of medicine, in his flanks and is symbolic of good health and well-being.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Dhanvant can be seen as a representation of good health, prosperity, and rejuvenation. It may serve as a reminder to protect and preserve one's health through various means, such as adhering to Ayurvedic practices, maintaining a balanced diet, practicing regular exercise, and engaging in spiritual practices. Additionally, it may be a source of inspiration and hope in challenging health conditions, reminding us that healing and recovery are always possible through divine intervention and inner strength.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dhanvant: One who possesses and protects wealth, symbolizing prosperity and abundance in one's life. The name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'dhan' (wealth) and 'vant' (protector).

vedic_reference.note: Name of Lord Dhanvantari, the physician of the gods.

historical_references.reference:
Dhanvantari, the god of Ayurveda, is mentioned in the ancient Hindu scripture, Charaka Samhita, which is believed to be composed between 1000 BCE and 500 BCE.
Context: Dhanvantari is considered the founder of Ayurveda, the ancient Indian system of medicine, and is depicted as carrying a bowl of elixir (amrit kalash) which symbolizes health and longevity.

King Dhanvantari of the Satavahana dynasty ruled between c. 130 BCE and 100 BCE.
Context: He is known for his successful military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms, and his reign marked a period of stability and prosperity for the Satavahana empire.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Dhanvant' is increasingly being seen on various tech and business platforms, often associated with professionals in the field of entrepreneurship and startups. Some notable individuals with this name include Dhanvant Sinha, a successful entrepreneur and investor who has been featured on AngelList and LinkedIn; and Dhanvant Patel, a renowned tech startup founder and mentor whose projects have been showcased on Crunchbase and other tech news sites.
